newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe hit with class action suit.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe hit with class action suit.

text.p: A lawsuit was filed against CompuServe Corp, certain of its officers, H&R Block Inc and its underwriters, seeking class action status, on behalf of anyone who, prior to July 16, 1996 purchased CompuServe stock, alleging CompuServe violated federal securities laws, a law firm said.
The plaintiff, Sonia Mitelman, is represented by Strauss & Troy, Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP, and Wolf Haldenstein Adler Freeman & Herz LLP, and other counsel.
The suit may be joined with a similar action that was filed in July 1996, against CompuServe.
CompuServe officials were not immediately available.
The suit alleges that the defendants failed to advise purchasers of CompuServe stock that the company was experiencing adverse trends that affected its growth rate.

On July 16, 1996, CompuServe projected a loss from operations of as much as $0.20 a share for its first fiscal quarter. CompuServe shares currently trade for substantially less - around 9-17/32 - than the $30 price at which they were sold in their initial public offering on April 18, 1996.
The suit was filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio.
CompuServe's underwriters in the IPO, Goldman Sachs & Co, George K. Baum & Co, and Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, were also named in the suit.
The plaintiff seeks damages on behalf of anyone who purchased CompuServe's stock on or traceable to its initial public offering, the law firms said.
CompuServe had been a unit of H&R Block.
